findings.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2 methods (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRoles*Permission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) throw UnsupportedOperationException unconditionally, converting previously-graceful V1 behavior into 500 errors for live callers such as the token-exchange flow (canExchangeTo with the AccessToken overload) and the per-client management/permissions admin REST endpoints; these should fail with a proper 4xx or no-op instead of an internal error

AdminPermissions removal-listener guard keys off the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ flag; when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is also enabled, management() resolves to MgmtPermissionsV2 and clients()/roles()/groups().setPermissionsEnabled(..., false) throw UnsupportedOperationException inside the ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent handlers, failing every client/role/group deletion server-wide; the guard should pin cleanup to the V1 implementation or the V2 implementations should no-op on cleanup

Secondary effect of the removal-listener guard: with the FGAP feature toggled off after V1 permissions were configured, removal cleanup no longer runs, leaving orphaned permission data that is inert but never cleaned

ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) materializes the 'Clients' type resource (and its scope definitions like configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) in the realm resource server as a write side effect of pure read/check paths (canView, canManage, canMapRoles), because the findByResource(...).isEmpty() short-circuit runs only after getResourceTypeResource has already created the resources, unlike hasPermission(String) which correctly uses findByName and creates nothing

All-clients MANAGE permission grants canManageClientScopes()/canManage(ClientScopeModel) but not canViewClientScopes()/canListClientScopes(), which only honor VIEW_CLIENTS/MANAGE_CLIENTS roles or the all-clients VIEW permission; a caller with manage-on-all-clients can update/delete realm client scopes by id but gets a 403 listing them, an inconsistency with canView(ClientScopeModel) which deliberately treats MANAGE as implying view

All-clients grants are silently ignored once a client has its own permission resource: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) in ClientPermissionsV2 binds evaluation to the per-client resource only, excluding policies attached to the Clients type resource, so admins holding all-clients MANAGE/VIEW/CONFIGURE grants silently lose access (403s) the moment a specific permission on that client is created; the identical pattern in UserPermissionsV2 likely affects users too

canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles in ClientPermissionsV2 check only the FGAP scope and drop the V1 canManage(client) implication, silently revoking role-mapping capability (user→client-role mapping, composite role assignment, client-scope role mapping) from admins with MANAGE_CLIENTS or FGAP MANAGE grants when V2 is enabled — a V1 parity break inconsistent with how canConfigure treats canManage in the same class

UnsupportedOperationException leaks as HTTP 500 from reachable endpoints: isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled and canExchangeTo in ClientPermissionsV2 are not gated by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check, so GET/POST /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions now throws 500 instead of the previously working V1 fall-through behavior; a 'not supported in V2' condition should surface as a clean 4xx, not a 500
With V2 enabled the removal listener does nothing and V2 has no equivalent, so FGAP resources/policies for deleted clients/roles/groups accumulate as orphans

getClientsWithPermission iterates findByType which now includes the type resource itself, adding the literal string 'Clients' to the result set alongside client UUIDs; any caller matching this set against client.getId() without special-casing the type resource will get zero matches for all-clients grants (deny-side)

Unbounded per-resource permission evaluation in getClientsWithPermission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:138-142): resourceStore.findByType is called with no limit/pagination and hasGrantedPermission runs a full evaluatePermission per returned resource, creating an O(N) N+1 evaluation shape with no batching, pagination, or per-request memoization — linear latency growth and DB/CPU amplification on the hot client list/search path as per-client grants accumulate

canView(client) triggers up to 4 independent full permission evaluations (all-clients VIEW, per-client MANAGE via canManage, CONFIGURE, per-client VIEW) with no per-request memoization, and each evaluation constructs the permission with resource.getScopes() so all 6 client scopes are processed even when only one is tested — repeated store lookups (resourceStore.findByName, getResourceTypeResource, PolicyStore.findByResource) that compound in aggregation methods like getAccess (~8-10 evaluations) and multiply with listing loops

All-clients permissions are silently ignored whenever a per-client resource exists in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission: the fallback to the type-level resource only happens when no per-client resource is found, causing false denials for admins with all-clients MANAGE/VIEW grants and bypassing Logic.NEGATIVE all-clients deny permissions when a per-client positive grant exists

getClientsWithPermission can return the literal string 'Clients' instead of client IDs because findByType matches the shared type-level resource, and realm-wide grants are never expanded to individual client IDs, causing consumers to hide/strip every client exactly when the admin has an all-clients grant

Removal-event cleanup (RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent) in AdminPermissions is now gated on the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag, leaving V2 with no cleanup path: deleting a client orphans its authz resource and associated permissions/policies; additionally, if both V1 and V2 flags are enabled, client deletion throws UnsupportedOperationException resulting in HTTP 500

V2 implementations (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) throw UnsupportedOperationException on externally reachable paths such as the management/permissions endpoints and token-exchange checks, surfacing as HTTP 500 instead of a clean 4xx/403/404 or false return

Wrong contract javadoc on requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() in ClientPermissionEvaluator: the docs claim the methods return true/false, but both are void and throw ForbiddenException on failure, which is incorrect for a public SPI interface

Inconsistent scope requirements for client-scope viewing under V2: canView(ClientScopeModel) accepts all-clients VIEW or MANAGE, but canViewClientScopes() only accepts VIEW, so an admin with all-clients MANAGE can manage individual client scopes but is denied listing client scopes

Removal-listener feature gate keys on the V1 flag (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) but management() dispatches to MgmtPermissionsV2 when V2 (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2) is enabled; with both features enabled, ClientRemovedEvent handling calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled which unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, failing the whole client deletion request (500, rollback) — a regression since the listener call was previously a harmless no-op via the inherited V1 ClientPermissions

No cleanup of V2 per-client authorization resources/permissions when a client is deleted in V2-only mode: the gated listener does nothing on ClientRemovedEvent, orphaning per-client resources (looked up via resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), ...)) and scope permissions; getClientsWithPermission() re-evaluates all orphaned resources via findByType and full evaluatePermission on every restricted client listing, causing a slow resource/policy leak and degrading performance of permission-filtered client listings

V1 client permission-management endpoints (GET/PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions) now return HTTP 500 instead of a graceful 'disabled' response when V2 is active: ClientPermissionsV2.isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled throw UnsupportedOperationException, breaking older consoles, admin CLI tooling, and custom automation that previously treated 'permissions disabled' as a normal state, while the sibling role/group endpoints still degrade gracefully

Behavioral change to removal-cleanup listener (now gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) ships with zero test coverage, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, making V2 cleanup impossible and leaving orphaned permission resources/policies on every client/role/group deletion

MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE is added to the schema and implemented in ClientPermissionsV2 but has no test coverage; testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and CONFIGURE together, so it doesn't isolate the scope under test and a regression in canMapClientScopeRoles would ship undetected

The large UnsupportedOperationException surface in ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) is untested; token exchange and the legacy per-client management/permissions endpoint could hit these paths under V2 and return 500s instead of proper denials

resolveClient's by-clientId fallback path (getClientByClientId) in AdminPermissionsSchema is never exercised by tests; all client permissions use the internal UUID, unlike the by-username resolution which is tested for users

No negative-logic (Logic.NEGATIVE) coverage for the Clients resource type; nothing verifies that a NEGATIVE client-scoped permission correctly overrides an all-clients grant, leaving deny-overrides-grant evaluation semantics unverified for clients

No scope/resourceType validation tests for the new Clients resource type; validation cases (missing resourceType, missing scopes, invalid scopes → BAD_REQUEST) are only tested for the Users type, so a regression allowing cross-type scopes for Clients would go unnoticed

Partial denial-boundary coverage for CONFIGURE and VIEW: the CONFIGURE test never asserts that client update/remove is denied, and the VIEW test doesn't assert update/delete/secret-regeneration denials, so over-grant regressions in canView/canConfigure/canManage boundaries would pass the suite

createClientPolicy helper added to AbstractPermissionTest but unused by any test, leaving the service-account-as-grantee scenario and client-policy evaluation path for the new Clients resource type unverified

Removal cleanup for the new CLIENTS resources has no V2 story: the ClientRemovedEvent handler calls setPermissionsEnabled, which throws UnsupportedOperationException in ClientPermissionsV2, and the Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) guard means the removal listener is silently skipped entirely in V2 mode

Deleting a client (or role/group) that has been granted permissions leaves orphaned Resource/Policy/Permission rows in the realm's admin-permissions resource server, which are then iterated and evaluated by getClientsWithPermission on every filtered listing
Latent crash path: if the flag wiring ever changes such that the removal listener runs while V2 is selected (e.g., both flags enabled), client/role/group deletion will fail with a 500

Three near-identical copies of the permission-evaluation/scope-scan logic in ClientPermissionsV2 (hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String), hasGrantedPermission) that have already diverged: only the per-client variant short-circuits when the all-clients resource has no attached policies, and hasGrantedPermission omits the isAdminSameRealm()/null-server guards its siblings have; extract a single hasGrantedScope(Resource, String) helper and reuse across V2 evaluators

Dead code: private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) in ClientPermissionsV2 is unreachable because every method that could use it (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission) throws UnsupportedOperationException; also unused in the same file are the logger field and the static import of TOKEN_EXCHANGE

Ten+ inherited interface methods in ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRoles*Permission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, is/setPermissionsEnabled, resource(), getPermissions()) are overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException, so callers holding ClientPermissionEvaluator/ClientPermissionManagement cannot tell which operations exist in V2 and the compiler will not flag new call sites; prefer a narrower V2 type so 'unsupported' is unrepresentable instead of a runtime throw

Wrong javadoc on requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() in ClientPermissionEvaluator: both are void methods that throw ForbiddenException, but the new javadoc says 'Returns true if canView()/canViewClientScopes() returns true' — copy-pasted from the can* methods

Type-level ('all clients') grants/denies are silently ignored once a client has its own resource: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) in ClientPermissionsV2.java:201-229 evaluates only one resource (per-client if it exists, otherwise the type resource), never both, causing silent loss of all-clients grants (e.g., MANAGE on all clients stops applying to a client once it gets a specific VIEW grant) and allowing deny-all permissions bound to the type resource to be bypassed by specific allows

No working cleanup path for V2 permission data when clients are deleted: the removal listener (AdminPermissions.java:77-91) is gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) and its only cleanup mechanism (clients().setPermissionsEnabled) throws UnsupportedOperationException in V2, so per-client resources and permissions created via getOrCreateResource are orphaned forever in the realm's admin-permissions resource server (or client deletion itself fails)

Orphaned resources and permissions accumulate unboundedly and permanently inflate a hot path: getClientsWithPermission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:124-144) iterates and evaluates permissions for every resource of type 'Clients' on every client-list call, so dead entries from deleted clients degrade performance and stale permissions remain visible/manageable via the permissions API

UnsupportedOperationException stubs in ClientPermissionsV2.java:146-199 (canExchangeTo, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource(), getPermissions(), and all *Permission() builders) are reachable from runtime paths: token-exchange requests reaching the FGAP check will surface as a 500 instead of a proper denial, per-client permissions endpoints will 500 instead of 4xx, and V1's token-exchange fine-grained capability is silently dropped with no V2 replacement

Permission checks now perform writes: the fallback in hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) at ClientPermissionsV2.java:211 calls getResourceTypeResource(...), which get-or-creates the 'Clients' type resource on read paths (e.g., client listing invoking canView/canManage per client), so a mere GET can mutate the admin-permissions resource server, concurrent first checks can race on resource creation, and this is inconsistent with the type-level hasPermission(String) which returns false when the type resource is absent

Feature-gating the removal listener in AdminPermissions.java:77 is a cleanup regression for the feature-off state: previously the role/client/group removal cleanup ran unconditionally, but now it only runs when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, so cleanup no longer occurs when the feature is off

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2 methods (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRoles*Permission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) throw UnsupportedOperationException unconditionally, converting previously-graceful V1 behavior into 500 errors for live callers such as the token-exchange flow (canExchangeTo with the AccessToken overload) and the per-client management/permissions admin REST endpoints; these should fail with a proper 4xx or no-op instead of an internal error

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the new `ClientPermissionsV2` class overrides multiple inherited methods and unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (e.g., `canExchangeTo(...)`, `exchangeToPermission(...)`, `managePermission(...)`, `configurePermission(...)`, `viewPermission(...)`, `isPermissionsEnabled(...)`, `setPermissionsEnabled(...)`, `resource(...)`, `getPermissions(...)`). `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is also changed to return this `ClientPermissionsV2`, so any V2 code path that calls these inherited methods will now fail via a runtime exception rather than a controlled/typed denial. However, the finding’s claim that this *definitely* converts “previously-graceful V1 behavior” into 500s for specific live callers (token exchange flow / admin REST endpoints) is not directly verifiable from this diff alone because no call sites are shown; reachability is plausible but not proven here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissions removal-listener guard keys off the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ flag; when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is also enabled, management() resolves to MgmtPermissionsV2 and clients()/roles()/groups().setPermissionsEnabled(..., false) throw UnsupportedOperationException inside the ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent handlers, failing every client/role/group deletion server-wide; the guard should pin cleanup to the V1 implementation or the V2 implementations should no-op on cleanup

adjudication.rationale: The listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener() now runs whenever Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled and, for ClientRemovedEvent, calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false). In this diff, MgmtPermissionsV2 overrides clients() to return ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). Therefore, if management(...) resolves to MgmtPermissionsV2 under any configuration where this listener is active (e.g., V2 permissions in use while ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled), client deletions will trigger an exception during cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Secondary effect of the removal-listener guard: with the FGAP feature toggled off after V1 permissions were configured, removal cleanup no longer runs, leaving orphaned permission data that is inert but never cleaned

ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) materializes the 'Clients' type resource (and its scope definitions like configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) in the realm resource server as a write side effect of pure read/check paths (canView, canManage, canMapRoles), because the findByResource(...).isEmpty() short-circuit runs only after getResourceTypeResource has already created the resources, unlike hasPermission(String) which correctly uses findByName and creates nothing

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when a per-client resource isn’t found (`resourceStore.findByName(...)` returns null), it calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` before checking whether any policies exist for that “all-clients” resource (`policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty()`). If `getResourceTypeResource` is a get-or-create (consistent with the schema’s `getOrCreateResource(...)` pattern added/extended in this diff), this introduces a write-side effect (materializing the Clients-type resource) on read/check code paths like `canView/canManage/canMapRoles`. By contrast, `hasPermission(String)` does a pure `findByName` and returns false if absent, creating nothing. The diff supports this asymmetry and the ordering concern; however, the exact create behavior of `getResourceTypeResource` isn’t shown in the diff, so impact is inferred from naming/patterns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: All-clients MANAGE permission grants canManageClientScopes()/canManage(ClientScopeModel) but not canViewClientScopes()/canListClientScopes(), which only honor VIEW_CLIENTS/MANAGE_CLIENTS roles or the all-clients VIEW permission; a caller with manage-on-all-clients can update/delete realm client scopes by id but gets a 403 listing them, an inconsistency with canView(ClientScopeModel) which deliberately treats MANAGE as implying view

adjudication.rationale: In the new V2 permission logic, `ClientPermissionsV2.canManageClientScopes()` returns true when the caller has the all-clients `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` permission (`return hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`). However, `ClientPermissionsV2.canView()` only checks `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` and does not treat MANAGE as implying VIEW. The interface docs state `canViewClientScopes()` is true iff `canView()` is true, and `canListClientScopes()` is also defined in terms of `canView()`/query roles. Since `ClientPermissionsV2` does not override `canViewClientScopes()`/`canListClientScopes()`, a caller with only all-clients MANAGE permission would be able to manage client scopes (`canManage(ClientScopeModel)` delegates to `canManageClientScopes()`), but still fail view/list checks that hinge on `canView()`. This matches the reported inconsistency and is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: All-clients grants are silently ignored once a client has its own permission resource: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) in ClientPermissionsV2 binds evaluation to the per-client resource only, excluding policies attached to the Clients type resource, so admins holding all-clients MANAGE/VIEW/CONFIGURE grants silently lose access (403s) the moment a specific permission on that client is created; the identical pattern in UserPermissionsV2 likely affects users too

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), if a per-client Resource exists (resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()) != null), evaluation is performed only against that per-client resource. The code consults the all-clients/type resource (AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)) only when the per-client resource is null. Therefore, once any client-specific permission causes creation of the per-client resource, any broader “all-clients” grants attached to the Clients type resource are no longer considered by this method, which can lead to unexpected 403s. The mention of UserPermissionsV2 cannot be verified from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles in ClientPermissionsV2 check only the FGAP scope and drop the V1 canManage(client) implication, silently revoking role-mapping capability (user→client-role mapping, composite role assignment, client-scope role mapping) from admins with MANAGE_CLIENTS or FGAP MANAGE grants when V2 is enabled — a V1 parity break inconsistent with how canConfigure treats canManage in the same class

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that in `ClientPermissionsV2` the methods `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` return only `hasPermission(client, <scope>)` and do not call `canManage(client)` (unlike `canConfigure`, which explicitly treats manage as implying configure). However, the finding’s key assertion—that this “drops the V1 canManage(client) implication” and therefore “silently revokes” role-mapping for admins with `MANAGE_CLIENTS` or FGAP `MANAGE`—is not supported by the diff: the updated `ClientPermissionEvaluator` Javadoc for these methods does not claim any `canManage`/`MANAGE_CLIENTS` implication for role-mapping, and the added tests (`PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient`) grant explicit MAP_ROLES(-*) scopes rather than relying on MANAGE. So the alleged V1 parity break cannot be verified from what’s shown and appears to be based on an assumption not evidenced in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UnsupportedOperationException leaks as HTTP 500 from reachable endpoints: isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled and canExchangeTo in ClientPermissionsV2 are not gated by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check, so GET/POST /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions now throws 500 instead of the previously working V1 fall-through behavior; a 'not supported in V2' condition should surface as a clean 4xx, not a 500

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces ClientPermissionsV2 where several ClientPermissionEvaluator methods (e.g., isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, canExchangeTo and multiple *Permission() methods) unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). MgmtPermissionsV2 is updated to return this ClientPermissionsV2 from clients(), so any existing REST/admin code path that calls these methods (notably client management-permissions enable/disable/status flows suggested by the method names) would now fail via an uncaught runtime exception, which typically propagates as HTTP 500 rather than a controlled 4xx/feature-not-supported response. No translation/guard is shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: With V2 enabled the removal listener does nothing and V2 has no equivalent, so FGAP resources/policies for deleted clients/roles/groups accumulate as orphans

getClientsWithPermission iterates findByType which now includes the type resource itself, adding the literal string 'Clients' to the result set alongside client UUIDs; any caller matching this set against client.getId() without special-casing the type resource will get zero matches for all-clients grants (deny-side)

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission`, the code iterates `resourceStore.findByType(..., AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and unconditionally adds `resource.getName()` to the returned set when the permission is granted. This diff also introduces an "all-clients" resource that is looked up by name `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` (i.e., literal "Clients") in `hasPermission(String scope)`. That implies the type-level resource is itself of type "Clients" and will be included by `findByType`, causing `getClientsWithPermission` to add the literal string "Clients" to the set rather than client UUIDs for an all-clients grant. Any consumer expecting the set to contain client IDs would not match `client.getId()` against "Clients".

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded per-resource permission evaluation in getClientsWithPermission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:138-142): resourceStore.findByType is called with no limit/pagination and hasGrantedPermission runs a full evaluatePermission per returned resource, creating an O(N) N+1 evaluation shape with no batching, pagination, or per-request memoization — linear latency growth and DB/CPU amplification on the hot client list/search path as per-client grants accumulate

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission, the code calls resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) and for every returned Resource invokes hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope), which calls root.evaluatePermission(...) per resource. This is an unbounded full scan over all client resources with per-item permission evaluation (O(N) evaluations, likely with DB/CPU cost), and there is no pagination/limit or caching/memoization visible in this diff. This is a concrete performance/scale concern introduced by the change, but not a functional correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canView(client) triggers up to 4 independent full permission evaluations (all-clients VIEW, per-client MANAGE via canManage, CONFIGURE, per-client VIEW) with no per-request memoization, and each evaluation constructs the permission with resource.getScopes() so all 6 client scopes are processed even when only one is tested — repeated store lookups (resourceStore.findByName, getResourceTypeResource, PolicyStore.findByResource) that compound in aggregation methods like getAccess (~8-10 evaluations) and multiply with listing loops

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2`, `canView(ClientModel client)` can indeed cascade into multiple separate permission evaluations with repeated store lookups. Specifically, it calls `canView()` (which may call `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)`), then `canConfigure(client)` (which calls `canManage(client)` -> `hasPermission(client, MANAGE)` and then `hasPermission(client, CONFIGURE)`), and if still false it finally calls `hasPermission(client, VIEW)`. Each `hasPermission...` builds `new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server)`, so the evaluation is performed over all scopes attached to the resource (for the clients resource type this is `Set.of(CONFIGURE, MANAGE, MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, VIEW)` per `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS`). There is no per-request memoization/cache visible in this diff, and each evaluation performs repeated `resourceStore.findByName(...)` plus, in the per-client variant, a fallback `getResourceTypeResource(...)` and `policyStore.findByResource(...)` check. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/architecture concern rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: All-clients permissions are silently ignored whenever a per-client resource exists in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission: the fallback to the type-level resource only happens when no per-client resource is found, causing false denials for admins with all-clients MANAGE/VIEW grants and bypassing Logic.NEGATIVE all-clients deny permissions when a per-client positive grant exists

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, the code evaluates permissions against exactly one `Resource`: it uses the per-client resource if `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())` returns non-null, and only falls back to the type-level ("all-clients") resource `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` when the per-client resource is missing. There is no additional evaluation/merge with the type-level resource when a per-client resource exists. Therefore any type-level grant/deny (including `Logic.NEGATIVE`) can be ignored whenever the per-client resource exists, causing incorrect allow/deny decisions as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission can return the literal string 'Clients' instead of client IDs because findByType matches the shared type-level resource, and realm-wide grants are never expanded to individual client IDs, causing consumers to hide/strip every client exactly when the admin has an all-clients grant
matched_golden_ids: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same core bug: getClientsWithPermission uses findByType on the shared type-level "Clients" resource and returns resource.getName(), yielding "Clients" (or otherwise non-client-ID values) rather than actual client IDs. This mismatches downstream expectations (client IDs for lookup/processing), leading to incorrect behavior (e.g., failing lookups or mis-filtering all clients).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal-event cleanup (RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent) in AdminPermissions is now gated on the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag, leaving V2 with no cleanup path: deleting a client orphans its authz resource and associated permissions/policies; additionally, if both V1 and V2 flags are enabled, client deletion throws UnsupportedOperationException resulting in HTTP 500
matched_golden_ids: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same core bug: the removal-event cleanup in AdminPermissions is incorrectly gated by the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ flag, so when only V2 is enabled the cleanup does not run and leaves orphaned authz/permission data. The extra note about UnsupportedOperationException is additional but does not change that it matches the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: V2 implementations (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) throw UnsupportedOperationException on externally reachable paths such as the management/permissions endpoints and token-exchange checks, surfacing as HTTP 500 instead of a clean 4xx/403/404 or false return

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides externally-invoked methods to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException(...)`, including `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel client, boolean enable)`. `AdminPermissions.registerListener` now runs (when `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled) and on `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false);`. With `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returning `new ClientPermissionsV2(...)`, that call will hit the overridden `setPermissionsEnabled` and throw, likely bubbling up as a runtime exception (HTTP 500 if occurring during an admin REST operation like client deletion). This is a concrete reachable path shown by the diff; other UOE methods may also be reachable but are not directly shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Wrong contract javadoc on requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() in ClientPermissionEvaluator: the docs claim the methods return true/false, but both are void and throw ForbiddenException on failure, which is incorrect for a public SPI interface

adjudication.rationale: In the diff for `ClientPermissionEvaluator`, the newly added Javadocs for `void requireView();` and `void requireViewClientScopes();` incorrectly state "Returns {@code true} if ..." even though both methods are `void` and (by naming/other docs like `requireManage()`/`requireList()`) are intended to throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding `can*` check is false. This is a real, diff-grounded SPI documentation/contract issue, but not a runtime correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent scope requirements for client-scope viewing under V2: canView(ClientScopeModel) accepts all-clients VIEW or MANAGE, but canViewClientScopes() only accepts VIEW, so an admin with all-clients MANAGE can manage individual client scopes but is denied listing client scopes

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2`, `canView(ClientScopeModel)` explicitly allows either all-clients `VIEW` or all-clients `MANAGE` permission (`return hasPermission(VIEW) || hasPermission(MANAGE);`). However, `canView()` in V2 only checks `hasPermission(VIEW)` (or `canViewClientDefault()`), and the interface contract for `canViewClientScopes()` states it returns true if `canView()` is true. This creates an inconsistency where a caller granted only all-clients `MANAGE` can be allowed to view/manage a specific `ClientScopeModel`, but may fail the higher-level “view/list client scopes” gate that relies on `canView()`/`canViewClientScopes()`, leading to denied listing of client scopes despite having `MANAGE`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal-listener feature gate keys on the V1 flag (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) but management() dispatches to MgmtPermissionsV2 when V2 (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2) is enabled; with both features enabled, ClientRemovedEvent handling calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled which unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, failing the whole client deletion request (500, rollback) — a regression since the listener call was previously a harmless no-op via the inherited V1 ClientPermissions

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener the removal listener now runs whenever Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, and for ClientRemovedEvent it calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false). This diff also introduces ClientPermissionsV2 where setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. MgmtPermissionsV2 is updated to return ClientPermissionsV2 from clients(), so if management(...) resolves to MgmtPermissionsV2 under any configuration where the listener is active, client deletion will trigger an exception (500/rollback) instead of a harmless no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cleanup of V2 per-client authorization resources/permissions when a client is deleted in V2-only mode: the gated listener does nothing on ClientRemovedEvent, orphaning per-client resources (looked up via resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), ...)) and scope permissions; getClientsWithPermission() re-evaluates all orphaned resources via findByType and full evaluatePermission on every restricted client listing, causing a slow resource/policy leak and degrading performance of permission-filtered client listings

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the ClientRemovedEvent listener now always calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). In V2, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, but `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)` is implemented as `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (services/.../ClientPermissionsV2.java). This makes client deletion events trigger an exception and prevents any disable/cleanup logic from running, which can leave per-client authz resources (looked up by `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), ...)`) orphaned and still discoverable via `resourceStore.findByType(...)` in `getClientsWithPermission()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: V1 client permission-management endpoints (GET/PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions) now return HTTP 500 instead of a graceful 'disabled' response when V2 is active: ClientPermissionsV2.isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled throw UnsupportedOperationException, breaking older consoles, admin CLI tooling, and custom automation that previously treated 'permissions disabled' as a normal state, while the sibling role/group endpoints still degrade gracefully

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces ClientPermissionsV2 and wires it in via MgmtPermissionsV2.clients(). In ClientPermissionsV2, core permission-management methods like isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel) and setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) are overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). If any existing REST endpoints or tooling paths still call these methods (e.g., the legacy client management/permissions endpoints), they would now fail with an unhandled runtime exception, which typically surfaces as HTTP 500 rather than a graceful "disabled"/false response. The diff itself shows the exception-throwing behavior and the new wiring, making the regression credible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change to removal-cleanup listener (now gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) ships with zero test coverage, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, making V2 cleanup impossible and leaving orphaned permission resources/policies on every client/role/group deletion

adjudication.rationale: The listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener now runs only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, but it still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) on ClientRemovedEvent. In this diff, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() is overridden to return ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). Therefore, when the feature is enabled and a client is removed, the cleanup listener will invoke a method that throws, breaking the removal-cleanup flow and preventing proper permission cleanup for client deletions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE is added to the schema and implemented in ClientPermissionsV2 but has no test coverage; testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and CONFIGURE together, so it doesn't isolate the scope under test and a regression in canMapClientScopeRoles would ship undetected

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds the new scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` to `AdminPermissionsSchema` and wires it into `CLIENTS` scopes, and implements authorization logic for it in `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` (which checks `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`). In the updated tests, `PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` grants `MAP_ROLES`, `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`, and `CONFIGURE` for the client, but never grants or asserts behavior for `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`. No other added/modified test in the diff appears to exercise `canMapClientScopeRoles`, so the finding about missing/insufficient test coverage for the new scope is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The large UnsupportedOperationException surface in ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) is untested; token exchange and the legacy per-client management/permissions endpoint could hit these paths under V2 and return 500s instead of proper denials

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new implementation `ClientPermissionsV2` and wires it in via `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` so V2 code will now return this class. In `ClientPermissionsV2`, many overridden methods explicitly `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, multiple `*Permission(...)` methods, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`). The added tests in `PermissionClientTest` exercise the new permission-evaluation paths (`canManage/canConfigure/canView/canMap*`) but do not cover any of the UnsupportedOperationException paths or assert that endpoints avoid calling them under V2. While the claim that token exchange/legacy endpoints will definitely hit these paths can’t be verified from this diff alone (no call sites shown), the unimplemented/exception-throwing surface area introduced and now reachable via `MgmtPermissionsV2` is a concrete, diff-grounded completeness/testing concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: resolveClient's by-clientId fallback path (getClientByClientId) in AdminPermissionsSchema is never exercised by tests; all client permissions use the internal UUID, unlike the by-username resolution which is tested for users

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient(...)`, the added fallback `session.clients().getClientByClientId(realm, id)` is only used when `id` is *not* an internal client UUID (i.e., when the caller passes a clientId like `"myclient"`). In the new/updated tests, client-specific permissions are created with `myclient.getId()` / `realmClient.getId()` (UUIDs), e.g. `createPermission(client, myclient.getId(), clientsType, Set.of(MANAGE), ...)` in `PermissionClientTest`, so the primary `getClientById` branch is exercised and the by-clientId fallback is not. This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing test/coverage issue for newly added logic, not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No negative-logic (Logic.NEGATIVE) coverage for the Clients resource type; nothing verifies that a NEGATIVE client-scoped permission correctly overrides an all-clients grant, leaving deny-overrides-grant evaluation semantics unverified for clients

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new Clients resource type and V2 evaluator logic (AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS + new scopes; ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(...) falls back to evaluating the all-clients resource when per-client resource is missing). New client-focused tests in PermissionClientTest cover positive grants (MANAGE/CONFIGURE/VIEW/MAP_ROLES/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE) but none create a Logic.NEGATIVE client permission to validate deny-overrides-grant behavior for clients, unlike UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest which explicitly tests a NEGATIVE permission overriding an all-users grant for impersonation. So the finding correctly identifies a missing, specific test for newly introduced nontrivial authorization behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No scope/resourceType validation tests for the new Clients resource type; validation cases (missing resourceType, missing scopes, invalid scopes → BAD_REQUEST) are only tested for the Users type, so a regression allowing cross-type scopes for Clients would go unnoticed

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `CLIENTS` resource type and new scopes in `AdminPermissionsSchema` (e.g., `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`, `CONFIGURE`, `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`) and wires it into the schema map. However, the existing REST validation tests in `PermissionRESTTest.permissionsTest()` still exercise BAD_REQUEST cases only for the Users type (missing resourceType, missing scopes, non-existent scopes) and were merely updated to call `createPermission(client, ...)` without adding equivalent cases for `CLIENTS`. The newly added `PermissionClientTest` focuses on authorization behavior (Forbidden vs allowed) rather than input validation. So there is a concrete, diff-grounded gap: no negative validation coverage specific to Clients-type scope/resourceType combinations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Partial denial-boundary coverage for CONFIGURE and VIEW: the CONFIGURE test never asserts that client update/remove is denied, and the VIEW test doesn't assert update/delete/secret-regeneration denials, so over-grant regressions in canView/canConfigure/canManage boundaries would pass the suite

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new client-scope permissions (CONFIGURE/VIEW/MANAGE etc.) and corresponding tests in `PermissionClientTest`, but the negative boundary coverage is incomplete as the finding states. In `testConfigureOnlyOneClient()`, after granting only `CONFIGURE` on a single client, the test asserts allowed secret operations and default-scope reads, and only asserts denial for adding/removing *default client scopes*; it does not assert that broader management actions like `clientResource.update(...)` or `clientResource.remove()` remain forbidden under CONFIGURE-only. In `testViewAllClients()`, after granting `VIEW` for all clients, it asserts denial for creating protocol mappers and creating a new client, but does not assert denial for other potentially over-granted operations such as updating/deleting clients or secret regeneration. Therefore, an over-grant regression in the canView/canConfigure/canManage boundary logic could plausibly pass this suite because these denials aren’t asserted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: createClientPolicy helper added to AbstractPermissionTest but unused by any test, leaving the service-account-as-grantee scenario and client-policy evaluation path for the new Clients resource type unverified

adjudication.rationale: In `AbstractPermissionTest` a new helper `createClientPolicy(...)` is added, but in the provided diff there are no call sites for it (tests shown use `createUserPolicy(...)` only, e.g., `PermissionClientTest`, `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest`). The new `Clients` resource type and V2 permission evaluation logic (`ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(...)`) are exercised via user-based policies/permissions, but the diff does not add any test that grants client permissions via a *client policy* (service account as grantee), so that client-policy evaluation path for the new Clients resource type remains unverified in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal cleanup for the new CLIENTS resources has no V2 story: the ClientRemovedEvent handler calls setPermissionsEnabled, which throws UnsupportedOperationException in ClientPermissionsV2, and the Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) guard means the removal listener is silently skipped entirely in V2 mode

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, the `ClientRemovedEvent` path calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). This diff also introduces `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returning `ClientPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (services/.../ClientPermissionsV2.java). If the V2 management implementation is used when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled (as suggested by the feature-guarded listener and the new V2 classes), deleting a client would trigger the listener and can crash with `UnsupportedOperationException`. The finding’s extra claim about the listener being “silently skipped entirely in V2 mode” isn’t directly provable from the diff, but the `setPermissionsEnabled`/V2 mismatch is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deleting a client (or role/group) that has been granted permissions leaves orphaned Resource/Policy/Permission rows in the realm's admin-permissions resource server, which are then iterated and evaluated by getClientsWithPermission on every filtered listing

adjudication.rationale: With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, the removal listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener now calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) on ClientRemovedEvent. In this diff, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns a ClientPermissionsV2 instance, but ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) is overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). Therefore client deletion will not clean up/disable any associated authz artifacts and may even throw during the event, leaving existing Resource/Policy/Permission data in the admin-permissions resource server. Separately, ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission iterates all resources of type CLIENTS via resourceStore.findByType(...) and evaluates permissions, so orphaned client resources/policies would continue to be iterated/evaluated during filtered listings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Latent crash path: if the flag wiring ever changes such that the removal listener runs while V2 is selected (e.g., both flags enabled), client/role/group deletion will fail with a 500

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a potential hard failure if the V2 permission implementation is ever used in the removal listener path. In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, when `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled it handles `ClientRemovedEvent` by calling `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`. However the new `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. If `management(...)` can return an instance whose `clients()` is `ClientPermissionsV2` (e.g., if V2 is selected while the listener is active), this would surface as an exception during deletion (likely a 500). The diff doesn’t show the feature/selector wiring that proves this is currently reachable, so it’s a concrete latent integration risk rather than a verified present bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Three near-identical copies of the permission-evaluation/scope-scan logic in ClientPermissionsV2 (hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String), hasGrantedPermission) that have already diverged: only the per-client variant short-circuits when the all-clients resource has no attached policies, and hasGrantedPermission omits the isAdminSameRealm()/null-server guards its siblings have; extract a single hasGrantedScope(Resource, String) helper and reuse across V2 evaluators

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2` there are three very similar scope-scan helpers: `hasPermission(ClientModel,String)`, `hasPermission(String)`, and `hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String)`. They already differ in behavior/guarding shown in the diff: the per-client method does an extra short-circuit when it falls back to the all-clients resource (`policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` -> `return false`), while `hasGrantedPermission` does not include the `root.isAdminSameRealm()` / `server == null` checks its siblings have (even though its current call site `getClientsWithPermission` performs those checks beforehand). This is a concrete maintainability/design issue introduced by the change (duplicated logic that has started to diverge), but not a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) in ClientPermissionsV2 is unreachable because every method that could use it (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission) throws UnsupportedOperationException; also unused in the same file are the logger field and the static import of TOKEN_EXCHANGE
matched_golden_ids: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is that ClientPermissionsV2 defines a private getEvaluationContext method that is never called and should be removed. The candidate explicitly flags getEvaluationContext as dead/unreachable/unused in ClientPermissionsV2 (even giving additional context and extra unused items), which is the same underlying issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Ten+ inherited interface methods in ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRoles*Permission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, is/setPermissionsEnabled, resource(), getPermissions()) are overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException, so callers holding ClientPermissionEvaluator/ClientPermissionManagement cannot tell which operations exist in V2 and the compiler will not flag new call sites; prefer a narrower V2 type so 'unsupported' is unrepresentable instead of a runtime throw

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ClientPermissionsV2 extends ClientPermissions` and explicitly overrides a large set of inherited methods to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `mapRoles*Permission`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`). This means code that is typed against the broader `ClientPermissions`/`ClientPermissionEvaluator` API can still compile and then fail at runtime if it calls one of these methods when `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returns a `ClientPermissionsV2`. The finding’s suggestion (use a narrower V2 type so unsupported operations are unrepresentable) is a valid design/architecture concern grounded in the shown implementation, even though the diff alone doesn’t prove an immediate failing call site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Wrong javadoc on requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() in ClientPermissionEvaluator: both are void methods that throw ForbiddenException, but the new javadoc says 'Returns true if canView()/canViewClientScopes() returns true' — copy-pasted from the can* methods

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionEvaluator, the newly added Javadoc for the void methods `requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` incorrectly states "Returns true..." even though these methods return `void` and are intended to throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding `can*` method is false. The diff shows this mismatch directly in the interface comments above those method declarations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Type-level ('all clients') grants/denies are silently ignored once a client has its own resource: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) in ClientPermissionsV2.java:201-229 evaluates only one resource (per-client if it exists, otherwise the type resource), never both, causing silent loss of all-clients grants (e.g., MANAGE on all clients stops applying to a client once it gets a specific VIEW grant) and allowing deny-all permissions bound to the type resource to be bypassed by specific allows

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)` the code selects exactly one `Resource` to evaluate: it looks up the per-client resource by `client.getId()` and only if that is `null` falls back to the type-level ("all clients") resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`). There is no path that evaluates both resources when both exist. Therefore any type-level grant/deny attached to the CLIENTS resource-type resource will be ignored for a client as soon as that client has its own resource (e.g., created by adding a per-client permission), and type-level denies can be bypassed by per-client allows. This behavior is directly implied by lines ~201-229 in the new file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No working cleanup path for V2 permission data when clients are deleted: the removal listener (AdminPermissions.java:77-91) is gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) and its only cleanup mechanism (clients().setPermissionsEnabled) throws UnsupportedOperationException in V2, so per-client resources and permissions created via getOrCreateResource are orphaned forever in the realm's admin-permissions resource server (or client deletion itself fails)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds V2 client permission evaluation (ClientPermissionsV2) but leaves all permission-management/cleanup APIs unsupported: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. Meanwhile, the deletion listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener() still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) on ClientRemovedEvent (now just wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)). If MgmtPermissionsV2 is in use (it now overrides clients() to return ClientPermissionsV2), client deletion events will trigger this call and hit the UnsupportedOperationException, breaking the intended cleanup path and potentially failing the deletion flow or leaving per-client authz resources/policies (which can be created via the new CLIENTS resource type and getOrCreateResource/resolveClient) orphaned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Orphaned resources and permissions accumulate unboundedly and permanently inflate a hot path: getClientsWithPermission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:124-144) iterates and evaluates permissions for every resource of type 'Clients' on every client-list call, so dead entries from deleted clients degrade performance and stale permissions remain visible/manageable via the permissions API

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces per-client authz resources of type "Clients" (AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE / CLIENTS) and a new ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission() that iterates *all* resources of that type and evaluates permissions for each (ClientPermissionsV2.java: ~95-140). The only cleanup hook shown for deleted clients is the AdminPermissions registerListener() handling ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), but in V2 that method is overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException (ClientPermissionsV2: setPermissionsEnabled). That means client deletion will not reliably disable/remove permissions/resources in V2, allowing orphaned entries to remain and grow, making getClientsWithPermission progressively slower and leaving stale permissions present in the authz store/permissions API.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UnsupportedOperationException stubs in ClientPermissionsV2.java:146-199 (canExchangeTo, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource(), getPermissions(), and all *Permission() builders) are reachable from runtime paths: token-exchange requests reaching the FGAP check will surface as a 500 instead of a proper denial, per-client permissions endpoints will 500 instead of 4xx, and V1's token-exchange fine-grained capability is silently dropped with no V2 replacement

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns the new `ClientPermissionsV2`, and that `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides multiple inherited methods (`canExchangeTo`, `*Permission(...)` builders, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`) to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. That is a concrete, diff-grounded concern: any runtime path that calls these methods while using V2 permissions would now crash rather than deny/return a 4xx. However, the finding’s stronger claims about specific reachability (token-exchange FGAP checks, per-client permissions endpoints) and “silently dropped” behavior are not verifiable from this diff alone because no call sites are shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission checks now perform writes: the fallback in hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) at ClientPermissionsV2.java:211 calls getResourceTypeResource(...), which get-or-creates the 'Clients' type resource on read paths (e.g., client listing invoking canView/canManage per client), so a mere GET can mutate the admin-permissions resource server, concurrent first checks can race on resource creation, and this is inconsistent with the type-level hasPermission(String) which returns false when the type resource is absent

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when the per-client Resource is missing it falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) (new code around the shown comment “check if there is permission for \"all-clients\"”). By contrast, hasPermission(String) uses resourceStore.findByName(...) and returns false if the type resource is absent. This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency in how the type-level resource is obtained, and it plausibly introduces an unintended side effect if getResourceTypeResource is implemented as “get-or-create” (the finding’s main concern). However, the diff does not include AuthorizationSchema.getResourceTypeResource implementation, so the claim that it definitely performs writes/races on read paths cannot be fully verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feature-gating the removal listener in AdminPermissions.java:77 is a cleanup regression for the feature-off state: previously the role/client/group removal cleanup ran unconditionally, but now it only runs when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, so cleanup no longer occurs when the feature is off

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes behavior in AdminPermissions.registerListener: all removal-handling branches (RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent) are now wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`, whereas previously they ran unconditionally. So the finding is accurate that cleanup will no longer run when the feature is off. However, from the diff alone it’s not verifiable that this is a *defect* (it may be intentional to only maintain fine-grained-authz artifacts when the feature is enabled), so it’s best treated as a review-significant behavioral change rather than a confirmed bug.
